It turned out to be true, but it was verified before writing the help box around it.","+- The admin console was never styled (`style.css` 404 on every nested admin page) through the entire build; nothing caught it — not the tests, not any review — until the required screenshots were taken (#13).","+","+[ADAM: which of these failures mattered most to you, and why — 2–3 sentences.]"]}],"originalFile":"# IPHS 400 — Mini-Project #2 starter (Web CMS)\n\nClick **Use this template** → name your repo **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** → make it **Public**.\nDo not fork: a fork arrives without an Issues tab, and your tickets live in Issues.\n\n## Start here\n\n1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. Read Part 0 and Part 1 first.\n2. `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` — how you are graded. Read it **before** you build.\n3. `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` — Exercise A, in Part 4 of the manual.\n\n## Run it\n\n```bash\nuv sync\ncp .env.example .env\nuv run cms serve        # then open http://localhost:8000/admin  -> \"T00: hello admin\"\n```\n\n## What is here\n\n```text\n.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger (Exercise A lives in ctx_guard.py)\nscripts/           usage_report.py (Exercise B lives in spend()), check_submission.py, seed_demo.py\ntests/             the exercise tests, plus helpers such as client_as(\"editor\")\napp/, templates/   the T00 skeleton — every CMS feature is yours to build\ndocs/adr/          two example decision records\n```\n\nTwo functions are deliberately unfinished and their tests fail until you write them:\n`decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` and `spend()` in `scripts/usage_report.py`.\nBoth are graded. Use `/tdd`, as the manual says.\n\n## Deadlines\n\nStage 1 (`mp2-mvp` tag): Tue Sep 29, 2:40 pm Eastern (soft target).\nStage 2 (`mp2-final` tag): Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern, grace until Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm.\n\nRun `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\n*(Required. Replace this section: name the models and skills you used, quote two\nprompts you really sent, describe one real model failure, and include a\n\"Backends used\" table if you ever switched providers.)*\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"99914136-bbd4-46d7-83fa-1bf47543bc7f","session_id":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

title, auto-generated slug (frozen once published), Markdown body, draft → pending → published status, author, timestamps, one Topic, any number of Tags.\n26\t4. **Pages** — a Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, plus standalone pages (About, Contact); Markdown is sanitized before render; nav is built from published pages; `cms publish` writes relative paths only.\n30\t\n31\tStretch features added beyond the required 7:\n32\t\n33\t- **Tags** — Staff-only creation, filterable within a Program, independent of Topic.\n34\t- **Search** — runs entirely client-side from a JSON index built at publish time, scoped to a section or sitewide, so it works on GitHub Pages with no server.\n35\t- **Media** — post covers and inline images set by the author; passwords hashed with argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.\n2. **Two roles** — **Staff** (`admin`) and **Ambassador** (`editor`), with genuinely different permissions: Staff can do everything an Ambassador can, plus publish, manage users, and manage the page tree.\n3. **Posts** — full CRUD; published pages appear in the public nav and breadcrumbs.\n5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a filterable content list, a post/page editor with a live preview.\n6. **User management** — Staff-only: create users, change roles, deactivate/reactivate; `uv run pytest -q` passed 226/226;\n`uv run cms serve` came up clean and `/` and `/admin` both returned HTTP 200. python3\n\"\"\"Screenshot pages with Playwright, for the design-review passes T11+ ask for.\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out notes/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --path / home \\\\\n        --path /asia/ asia\n\nStarts the real app (`app.main:app`) on a throwaway port, waits for it to\ncome up, then drives headless Chromium to capture each --path at each\n--width as \"<name>-<width>.png\" under --out. Pass --login EMAIL PASSWORD to\nauthenticate first (needed for admin screenshots).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport socket\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport urllib.request\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef _free_port() -> int:\n    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:\n        s.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\n        return s.getsockname()[1]\n\n\ndef _wait_for(url: str, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:\n    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout\n    while time.monotonic() < deadline:\n        try:\n            urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=1)\n            return\n        except OSError:\n            time.sleep(0.2)\n    raise RuntimeError(f\"server never came up at {url}\")\n\n\ndef _login(page, base: str, email: str, password: str) -> None:\n    page.goto(base + \"/login\", wait_until=\"networkidle\")\n    token = page.get_attribute('input[name=\"csrf_token\"]', \"value\")\n    page.fill('input[name=\"email\"]', email)\n    page.fill('input[name=\"password\"]', password)\n    page.click('button[type=\"submit\"]')\n    page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\")\n    if token is None:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"login page had no csrf_token field\")\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True, type=Path)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--widths\", nargs=\"+\", type=int, default=[1280, 390])\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--path\", nargs=2, action=\"append\", metavar=(\"URL_PATH\", \"NAME\"),\n        default=[], dest=\"paths\", help=\"repeatable: a URL path and a filename stem\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--login\", nargs=2, metavar=(\"EMAIL\", \"PASSWORD\"), default=None,\n        help=\"log in with these creds before screenshotting\",\n    )\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if not args.paths:\n        parser.error(\"pass at least one --path URL_PATH NAME\")\n\n    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    port = _free_port()\n    base = f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\"\n\n    server = subprocess.Popen(\n        [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"uvicorn\", \"app.main:app\", \"--port\", str(port)],\n        cwd=ROOT,\n    )\n    try:\n        _wait_for(base + \"/\")\n        with sync_playwright() as p:\n            browser = p.chromium.launch()\n            for width in args.widths:\n                context = browser.new_context(viewport={\"width\": width, \"height\": 900})\n                page = context.new_page()\n                if args.login:\n                    _login(page, base, *args.login)\n                for url_path, name in args.paths:\n                    page.goto(base + url_path, wait_until=\"networkidle\")\n                    page.screenshot(path=str(args.out / f\"{name}-{width}.png\"), full_page=True)\n                context.close()\n            browser.close()\n    finally:\n        server.terminate()\n        try:\n            server.wait(timeout=10)\n        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n            server.kill()\n            server.wait(timeout=10)\n\n    print(f\"Saved screenshots to {args.out}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, media, pages, posts, public, tags\nfrom app.routes.auth import AdminRequired, CsrfInvalid, LoginRequired\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    db.init_db()\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                        session_cookie=\"cms_session\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def _login_required(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(url=\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(AdminRequired)\n    def _admin_required(request: Request, exc: AdminRequired):\n        return PlainTextResponse(\"Forbidden\", status_code=403)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(CsrfInvalid)\n    def _csrf_invalid(request: Request, exc: CsrfInvalid):\n        return PlainTextResponse(\"Forbidden: missing or invalid CSRF token\", status_code=403)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(tags.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(media.router)\n\n    # Catch-all last: the live public site, read straight from the database —\n    # the admin console's \"preview\" of what `cms publish` will later export.\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app","numLines":50,"startLine":1,"totalLines":54}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2808c8b5-b8b4-419a-9f0d-393d1186ab96","session_id":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

Pass --login EMAIL PASSWORD to\nauthenticate first (needed for admin screenshots).\n\nThe 6 screens check_submission.py --stage 2 requires in docs/screenshots/\n(\"{screen}-{1280|390}.png\" for screen in login, dashboard, content-list,\neditor, users, editor-denied) — pass these --path/name pairs exactly so the\noutput filenames match:\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out docs/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --path /login login \\\\\n        --login admin@example.test change-me-admin \\\\\n        --path /admin/dashboard dashboard \\\\\n        --path /admin/content content-list \\\\\n        --path /admin/posts/new editor \\\\\n        --path /admin/accounts users\n\nThen a second run, logged in as an editor (Ambassador), to capture the\nStaff-only page being refused:\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out docs/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --login editor@example.test change-me-editor \\\\\n        --path /admin/accounts editor-denied\n\"\"\"","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Screenshot pages with Playwright, for the design-review passes T11+ ask for.\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out notes/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --path / home \\\\\n        --path /asia/ asia\n\nStarts the real app (`app.main:app`) on a throwaway port, waits for it to\ncome up, then drives headless Chromium to capture each --path at each\n--width as \"<name>-<width>.png\" under --out. Pass --login EMAIL PASSWORD to\nauthenticate first (needed for admin screenshots).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport socket\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport urllib.request\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef _free_port() -> int:\n    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:\n        s.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\n        return s.getsockname()[1]\n\n\ndef _wait_for(url: str, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:\n    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout\n    while time.monotonic() < deadline:\n        try:\n            urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=1)\n            return\n        except OSError:\n            time.sleep(0.2)\n    raise RuntimeError(f\"server never came up at {url}\")\n\n\ndef _login(page, base: str, email: str, password: str) -> None:\n    page.goto(base + \"/login\", wait_until=\"networkidle\")\n    token = page.get_attribute('input[name=\"csrf_token\"]', \"value\")\n    page.fill('input[name=\"email\"]', email)\n    page.fill('input[name=\"password\"]', password)\n    page.click('button[type=\"submit\"]')\n    page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\")\n    if token is None:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"login page had no csrf_token field\")\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True, type=Path)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--widths\", nargs=\"+\", type=int, default=[1280, 390])\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--path\", nargs=2, action=\"append\", metavar=(\"URL_PATH\", \"NAME\"),\n        default=[], dest=\"paths\", help=\"repeatable: a URL path and a filename stem\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--login\", nargs=2, metavar=(\"EMAIL\", \"PASSWORD\"), default=None,\n        help=\"log in with these creds before screenshotting\",\n    )\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if not args.paths:\n        parser.error(\"pass at least one --path URL_PATH NAME\")\n\n    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    port = _free_port()\n    base = f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\"\n\n    server = subprocess.Popen(\n        [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"uvicorn\", \"app.main:app\", \"--port\", str(port)],\n        cwd=ROOT,\n    )\n    try:\n        _wait_for(base + \"/\")\n        with sync_playwright() as p:\n            browser = p.chromium.launch()\n            for width in args.widths:\n                context = browser.new_context(viewport={\"width\": width, \"height\": 900})\n                page = context.new_page()\n                if args.login:\n                    _login(page, base, *args.login)\n                for url_path, name in args.paths:\n                    page.goto(base + url_path, wait_until=\"networkidle\")\n                    page.screenshot(path=str(args.out / f\"{name}-{width}.png\"), full_page=True)\n                context.close()\n            browser.close()\n    finally:\n        server.terminate()\n        try:\n            server.wait(timeout=10)\n        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n            server.kill()\n            server.wait(timeout=10)\n\n    print(f\"Saved screenshots to {args.out}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":10,"oldLines":6,"newStart":10,"newLines":28,"lines":[" come up, then drives headless Chromium to capture each --path at each"," --width as \"<name>-<width>.png\" under --out.       --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --login editor@example.test change-me-editor \\\\\n        --path /admin/accounts editor-denied\n\"\"\"","originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Screenshot pages with Playwright, for the design-review passes T11+ ask for.\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out notes/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --path / home \\\\\n        --path /asia/ asia\n\nStarts the real app (`app.main:app`) on a throwaway port, waits for it to\ncome up, then drives headless Chromium to capture each --path at each\n--width as \"<name>-<width>.png\" under --out. Pass --login EMAIL PASSWORD to\nauthenticate first (needed for admin screenshots).\n\nThe 6 screens check_submission.py --stage 2 requires in docs/screenshots/\n(\"{screen}-{1280|390}.png\" for screen in login, dashboard, content-list,\neditor, users, editor-denied) — pass these --path/name pairs exactly so the\noutput filenames match:\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out docs/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --path /login login \\\\\n        --login admin@example.test change-me-admin \\\\\n        --path /admin/dashboard dashboard \\\\\n        --path /admin/content content-list \\\\\n        --path /admin/posts/new editor \\\\\n        --path /admin/accounts users\n\nThen a second run, logged in as an editor (Ambassador), to capture the\nStaff-only page being refused:\n\n    uv run python scripts/screenshot.py --out docs/screenshots \\\\\n        --widths 1280 390 \\\\\n        --login editor@example.test change-me-editor \\\\\n        --path /admin/accounts editor-denied\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport socket\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport urllib.request\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef _free_port() -> int:\n    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:\n        s.bind((\"127.0.0.1\", 0))\n        return s.getsockname()[1]\n\n\ndef _wait_for(url: str, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:\n    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout\n    while time.monotonic() < deadline:\n        try:\n            urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=1)\n            return\n        except OSError:\n            time.sleep(0.2)\n    raise RuntimeError(f\"server never came up at {url}\")\n\n\ndef _login(page, base: str, email: str, password: str) -> None:\n    page.goto(base + \"/login\", wait_until=\"networkidle\")\n    token = page.get_attribute('input[name=\"csrf_token\"]', \"value\")\n    page.fill('input[name=\"email\"]', email)\n    page.fill('input[name=\"password\"]', password)\n    page.click('button[type=\"submit\"]')\n    page.wait_for_load_state(\"networkidle\")\n    if token is None:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"login page had no csrf_token field\")\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--out\", required=True, type=Path)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--widths\", nargs=\"+\", type=int, default=[1280, 390])\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--path\", nargs=2, action=\"append\", metavar=(\"URL_PATH\", \"NAME\"),\n        default=[], dest=\"paths\", help=\"repeatable: a URL path and a filename stem\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--login\", nargs=2, metavar=(\"EMAIL\", \"PASSWORD\"), default=None,\n        help=\"log in with these creds before screenshotting\",\n    )\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if not args.paths:\n        parser.error(\"pass at least one --path URL_PATH NAME\")\n\n    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    port = _free_port()\n    base = f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\"\n\n    server = subprocess.Popen(\n        [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"uvicorn\", \"app.main:app\", \"--port\", str(port)],\n        cwd=ROOT,\n    )\n    try:\n        _wait_for(base + \"/\")\n        with sync_playwright() as p:\n            browser = p.chromium.launch()\n            for width in args.widths:\n                context = browser.new_context(viewport={\"width\": width, \"height\": 900})\n                page = context.new_page()\n                if args.login:\n                    _login(page, base, *args.login)\n                for url_path, name in args.paths:\n                    page.goto(base + url_path, wait_until=\"networkidle\")\n                    page.screenshot(path=str(args.out / f\"{name}-{width}.png\"), full_page=True)\n                context.close()\n            browser.close()\n    finally:\n        server.terminate()\n        try:\n            server.wait(timeout=10)\n        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:\n            server.kill()\n            server.wait(timeout=10)\n\n    print(f\"Saved screenshots to {args.out}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":14,"oldLines":18,"newStart":14,"newLines":21,"lines":[" The 6 screens check_submission.py fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import models, settings\nfrom app.services import csrf, passwords\nfrom app.services.css_path import css_path_for\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\nGENERIC_LOGIN_ERROR = \"Incorrect email or password.\"\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `require_user` for an anonymous request; caught in app/main.py.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass AdminRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `require_admin` for a non-admin request; caught in app/main.py.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass CsrfInvalid(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `verify_csrf` for a missing or wrong token; caught in app/main.py.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef ensure_csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Make sure the session has a CSRF token, and return it for the form.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    if not token:\n        token = csrf.generate_token()\n        request.session[\"csrf_token\"] = token\n    return token\n\n\nasync def verify_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    form = await request.form()\n    submitted = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    session_token = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    if not csrf.tokens_match(session_token, submitted):\n        raise CsrfInvalid()\n\n\ndef get_current_user(request: Request) -> models.User | None:\n    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    if user_id is None:\n        return None\n    user = models.get_user_by_id(user_id)\n    if user is None or not user.active:\n        return None\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_user(request: Request) -> models.User:\n    user = get_current_user(request)\n    if user is None:\n        raise LoginRequired()\n    return user\n\n\ndef require_admin(user: models.User = Depends(require_user)) -> models.User:\n    if user.role != \"admin\":\n        raise AdminRequired()\n    return user\n\n\n@router.get(\"/login\")\ndef login_form(request: Request):\n    token = ensure_csrf_token(request)\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/login.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Log in\", \"csrf_token\": token, \"error\": None,\n         \"css_path\": css_path_for(request)},\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/login\")\nasync def login_submit(\n    request: Request,\n    email: str = Form(...),\n    password: str = Form(...),\n    _csrf: None = Depends(verify_csrf),\n):\n    user = models.get_user_by_email(email)\n    if user is None or not user.active or not ensure_csrf_token(request)\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/login.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Log in\", \"csrf_token\": token, \"error\": request.session[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf.generate_token()\n    return RedirectResponse(url=\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/logout\")\nasync def logout(request: Request, _csrf: None = Depends(verify_csrf)):\n    request.session.clear()\n    return RedirectResponse(url=\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin/_stub\")\ndef admin_only_stub(request: Request, user: models.User = Depends(require_admin)):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/stub.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Admin-only stub\", \"user\": user, \"css_path\": Ambassador console shell (T08, #9):\n3\tthe \"My posts\" landing screen.\n4\t\n5\tEvery route but the landing screen is admin-only (require_admin, same gate\n6\tas Pages and Accounts) — an Ambassador gets a 403, an anonymous request is\n7\tredirected to /login. Page hierarchy and Accounts are their own existing\n8\trouters (app/routes/pages.py, app/routes/accounts.py); this module only adds\n9\tthe sidebar entries that point at them.\n10\t\n11\tThe landing screen (GET /admin) stays open to any logged-in user: Staff see\n12\tthe live preview described below; an Ambassador sees \"My posts\" — their own\n13\tPosts grouped by status, nothing else — which doubles as their entire\n14\tsidebar (plus logout), since every other console route is admin-only.\n15\t\"\"\"\n16\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n17\t\n18\tfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\n19\tfrom fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse\n20\tfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n21\t\n22\tfrom app import models, settings\n23\tfrom app.routes.auth import get_current_user, require_admin\n24\tfrom app.routes.public import page_context\n25\tfrom app.services import console_shell, review_gate\n26\t\n27\ttemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n28\t\n29\trouter = APIRouter()\n30\t\n31\tSTATUS_CHOICES = [\"draft\", \"pending\", \"published\"]\n32\tTYPE_CHOICES = [(\"page\", \"Page\"), (\"post\", \"Post\")]\n33\t\n34\t\n35\t@router.get(\"/style.css\")\n36\tdef admin_stylesheet() -> PlainTextResponse:\n37\t    \"\"\"The admin console's stylesheet (issue #13) — every admin template\n38\t    links here with a relative, depth-computed href (console_shell.css_path_for),\n39\t    since a literal root-absolute href would fail check_submission.py's scan\n40\t    of every tracked template, live-server-only or not.\"\"\"\n41\t    return PlainTextResponse(console_shell.ADMIN_CSS, media_type=\"text/css\")\n42\t\n43\t\n44\tdef _my_posts_response(request: Request, user: models.User):\n45\t    \"\"\"An Ambassador's own Posts, grouped by status — nothing belonging to\n46\t    anyone else. A Post is only editable/deletable while draft (same rule\n47\t    app/routes/posts.py enforces), so edit/delete links only render there;\n48\t    `review_gate.available_actions` supplies the rest (submit, for a draft).\"\"\"\n49\t    own_posts = models.list_posts_by_author(user.id)\n50\t    groups = []\n51\t    for status in STATUS_CHOICES:\n52\t        rows = []\n53\t        for post in sorted(\n54\t            (p for p in own_posts if p.status == status),\n55\t            key=lambda p: p.updated_at,\n56\t            reverse=True,\n57\t        ):\n58\t            program = models.get_page_by_id(post.program_id)\n59\t            rows.append({\n60\t                \"post\": post,\n61\t                \"program_title\": program.title if program else \"Unknown program\",\n62\t                \"edit_href\": f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/edit\",\n63\t                \"delete_href\": f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/delete\",\n64\t                \"can_edit\": status == \"draft\",\n65\t                \"actions\": [\n66\t                    (action, review_gate.ACTION_LABELS[action], f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/{action}\")\n67\t                    for action in review_gate.available_actions(status, user.role, True)\n68\t                ],\n69\t            })\n70\t        groups.append({\"status\": status, \"rows\": rows})\n71\t\n72\t    context = console shell (T07, #8): the live-preview landing screen, Dashboard,\nContent list, Pending queue, and Metrics. Ambassador console shell (T08, #9):\nthe \"My posts\" landing screen.\n\nEvery route but the landing screen is admin-only (require_admin, same gate\nas Pages and Accounts) — an Ambassador gets a 403, an anonymous request is\nredirected to /login. Page hierarchy and Accounts are their own existing\nrouters (app/routes/pages.py, app/routes/accounts.py); this module only adds\nthe sidebar entries that point at them.\n\nThe landing screen (GET /admin) stays open to any logged-in user: Staff see\nthe live preview described below; an Ambassador sees \"My posts\" — their own\nPosts grouped by status, nothing else — which doubles as their entire\nsidebar (plus logout), since every other console route is admin-only.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import models, settings\nfrom app.routes.auth import get_current_user, require_admin\nfrom app.routes.public import page_context\nfrom app.services import console_shell, review_gate\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\nSTATUS_CHOICES = [\"draft\", \"pending\", \"published\"]\nTYPE_CHOICES = [(\"page\", \"Page\"), (\"post\", \"Post\")]\n\n\n@router.get(\"/style.css\")\ndef admin_stylesheet() -> PlainTextResponse:\n    \"\"\"The admin console's stylesheet (issue #13) — every admin template\n    links here with a relative, depth-computed href (console_shell.css_path_for),\n    since a literal root-absolute href would fail check_submission.py's scan\n    of every tracked template, live-server-only or not.\"\"\"\n    return PlainTextResponse(console_shell.ADMIN_CSS, media_type=\"text/css\")\n\n\ndef _my_posts_response(request: Request, user: models.User):\n    \"\"\"An Ambassador's own Posts, grouped by status — nothing belonging to\n    anyone else. A Post is only editable/deletable while draft (same rule\n    app/routes/posts.py enforces), so edit/delete links only render there;\n    `review_gate.available_actions` supplies the rest (submit, for a draft).\"\"\"\n    own_posts = models.list_posts_by_author(user.id)\n    groups = []\n    for status in STATUS_CHOICES:\n        rows = []\n        for post in sorted(\n            (p for p in own_posts if p.status == status),\n            key=lambda p: p.updated_at,\n            reverse=True,\n        ):\n            program = models.get_page_by_id(post.program_id)\n            rows.append({\n                \"post\": post,\n                \"program_title\": program.title if program else \"Unknown program\",\n                \"edit_href\": f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/edit\",\n                \"delete_href\": f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/delete\",\n                \"can_edit\": status == \"draft\",\n                \"actions\": [\n                    (action, review_gate.ACTION_LABELS[action], f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/{action}\")\n                    for action in review_gate.available_actions(status, user.role, True)\n                ],\n            })\n        groups.append({\"status\": status, \"rows\": rows})\n\n    context = console_shell.console_context(request, user, sidebar=console_shell.EDITOR_SIDEBAR)\n    context.update({\"title\": \"My posts\", \"groups\": groups})\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/my_posts.html\", context)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin\")\ndef admin_home(request: Request, user: models.User | None = Depends(get_current_user)):\n    if user is None:\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"user\": None, \"csrf_token\": None,\n             \"css_path\": console_shell.css_path_for(request)},\n        )\n    if user.role != \"admin\":\n        return _my_posts_response(request, user)\n\n    home_page = models.ensure_home_page()\n    context = console_shell.console_context(request, user)\n    context.update({\"title\": \"Admin — Live preview\", \"preview\": page_context(home_page)})\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/home.html\", context)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin/dashboard\")\ndef dashboard(request: Request, user: models.User = Depends(require_admin)):\n    posts = models.list_all_posts()\n    status_counts = {status: 0 for status in STATUS_CHOICES}\n    for post in posts:\n        status_counts[post.status] += 1\n\n    level_counts: dict[int, int] = {}\n    for page in models.list_all_pages():\n        level = len(models.list_ancestors(page))\n        level_counts[level] = level_counts.get(level, 0) + 1\n\n    context = console_shell.console_context(request, user)\n    context.update({\n        \"title\": \"Dashboard\",\n        \"status_counts\": [(status, status_counts[status]) for status in STATUS_CHOICES],\n        \"level_counts\": sorted(level_counts.items()),\n        \"active_accounts\": sum(1 for u in models.list_users() if u.active),\n    })\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/dashboard.html\", context)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin/content\")\ndef content_list(\n    request: Request,\n    user: models.User = Depends(require_admin),\n    status: str = \"\",\n    kind: str = \"\",\n):\n    items = []\n    if kind in (\"\", \"page\"):\n        for page in models.list_all_pages():\n            if status and page.status != status:\n                continue\n            items.append({\n                \"kind\": \"Page\", \"title\": page.title, \"status\": page.status,\n                \"href\": f\"/admin/pages/{page.id}/edit\",\n            })\n    if kind in (\"\", \"post\"):\n        for post in models.list_all_posts():\n            if status and post.status != status:\n                continue\n            items.append({\n                \"kind\": \"Post\", \"title\": post.title, \"status\": post.status,\n                \"href\": f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/edit\",\n            })\n\n    context = console_shell.console_context(request, user)\n    context.update({\n        \"title\": \"Content list\",\n        \"items\": items,\n        \"status_choices\": STATUS_CHOICES,\n        \"type_choices\": TYPE_CHOICES,\n        \"status_filter\": status,\n        \"kind_filter\": kind,\n    })\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/content_list.html\", context)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin/pending\")\ndef pending_queue(request: Request, user: models.User = Depends(require_admin)):\n    pending = sorted(\n        (p for p in models.list_all_posts() if p.status == \"pending\"),\n        key=lambda p: p.updated_at,\n    )\n    rows = []\n    for post in pending:\n        author = models.get_user_by_id(post.author_id) if post.author_id else None\n        rows.append({\n            \"post\": post,\n            \"author_name\": author.display_name if author else \"Unknown\",\n            \"submitted_date\": (post.updated_at or \"\")[:10],\n            \"edit_href\": f\"/admin/posts/{post.id}/edit\",\n        })\n\n    context = console_shell.console_context(request, user)\n    context.update({\"title\": \"Pending queue\", \"rows\": rows})\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/pending_queue.html\", context)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin/metrics\")\ndef metrics(request: Request, user: models.User = Depends(require_admin)):\n    programs = [p for p in models.list_all_pages() if models.is_program_page(p)]\n    rows = sorted(\n        (\n            {\"program\": program, \"count\": len(models.list_posts_by_program(program.id))}\n            for program in programs\n        ),\n        key=lambda row: row[\"program\"].title,\n    )\n\n    context = console_shell.console_context(request, user)\n    context.update({\"title\": \"Metrics\", \"rows\": rows})\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/metrics.html\", context)\n","numLines":188,"startLine":1,"totalLines":188}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0a2f1150-c01b-409e-b1b1-6ddb8ad0beb6","session_id":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

Every\n3\t`app/routes/*.py` module except `public.py` uses this (the public site has\n4\tits own, unrelated live-preview chrome in `app/routes/public.py`).\n5\t\n6\tIssue #13: the admin console's stylesheet link is relative and\n7\tdepth-computed (see app.services.css_path) rather than root-absolute —\n8\ta literal `href=\"/...\"` would still work on this live server, but\n9\t`scripts/check_submission.py` greps every tracked template for\n10\troot-absolute paths regardless of whether the page is ever statically\n11\texported, so this stays relative like everything else.\n12\t\"\"\"\n13\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n14\t\n15\tfrom urllib.parse import quote\n16\t\n17\tfrom fastapi import Request\n18\tfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n19\t\n20\tfrom app import models\n21\tfrom app.routes.auth import ensure_csrf_token\n22\tfrom app.services.css_path import css_path_for\n23\t\n24\tSIDEBAR = [\n25\t    (\"/admin/dashboard\", \"Dashboard\"),\n26\t    (\"/admin/content\", \"Content list\"),\n27\t    (\"/admin/pending\", \"Pending queue\"),\n28\t    (\"/admin/accounts\", \"Accounts\"),\n29\t    (\"/admin/pages\", \"Page hierarchy\"),\n30\t    (\"/admin/tags\", \"Tags\"),\n31\t    (\"/admin/metrics\", \"Metrics\"),\n32\t]\n33\t\n34\tEDITOR_SIDEBAR = [\n35\t    (\"/admin\", \"My posts\"),\n36\t]\n37\t\n38\t\n39\tdef console_context(request: Request, user: models.User, sidebar=None) -> dict:\n40\t    \"\"\"The csrf token, stylesheet path, and sidebar every authenticated\n41\t    admin screen needs. Defaults the sidebar by role (Staff vs Ambassador)\n42\t    so most call sites don't have to pick one themselves.\"\"\"\n43\t    chosen = sidebar or (SIDEBAR if user.role == \"admin\" else EDITOR_SIDEBAR)\n44\t    return {\n45\t        \"user\": user,\n46\t        \"csrf_token\": ensure_csrf_token(request),\n47\t        \"css_path\": css_path_for(request),\n48\t        \"sidebar\": [{\"href\": href, \"label\": label} for href, label in chosen],\n49\t    }\n50\t\n51\t\n52\tdef redirect_with_flash(\n53\t    url: str, message: str, *, fragment: str | None = None, **extra_params: str\n54\t) -> RedirectResponse:\n55\t    \"\"\"A 303 redirect carrying a one-time success message, read back by\n56\t    templates/base.html's `request.query_params`. No session state: a\n57\t    refresh of the destination page just drops the message, which is fine\n58\t    for a \"your save worked\" banner.\n59\t\n60\t    `fragment` and `extra_params` (#15 follow-up) let a caller land the\n61\t    reader on a specific part of a long page — e.g. an image upload redirect\n62\t    jumps straight to that upload section instead of the top of the post\n63\t    form, with `extra_params` carrying which Media was just added so the\n64\t    template can show its thumbnail there. The fragment is appended last,\n65\t    since a URL fragment must come after the query string to be valid.\n66\t    \"\"\"\n67\t    sep = \"&\" if \"?\" in url else \"?\"\n68\t    target = f\"{url}{sep}flash={quote(message)}\"\n69\t    for key, value in extra_params.items():\n70\t        target += f\"&{key}={quote(str(value))}\"\n71\t    if fragment:\n72\t        target += f\"#{fragment}\"\n73\t    return RedirectResponse(url=target, status_code=303)\n74\t\n75\t\n76\t# Reuses the public site's Kenyon purple + gold palette and Fraunces/Inter\n77\t# fonts (app/publish.py's CSS) for a consistent look, but is otherwise\n78\t# self-contained: the admin console's HTML (sidebar, forms, plain <ul> lists\n79\t# standing in for tables) is different enough from the public site's that\n80\t# sharing one stylesheet would mean every admin rule risks colliding with a\n81\t# public one, or vice versa.\n82\tADMIN_CSS = \"\"\"/* Admin console shell — issue #13. Same palette/fonts as the\n83\t   public site (app/publish.py's CSS), different components: a sidebar\n84\t   layout, plain lists standing in for tables, and HTML forms. */\n85\t:root {\n86\t  color-scheme: light dark;\n87\t  --purple: #5B2A86;\n88\t  --purple-dark: #3E1C5E;\n89\t  --purple-light: #F2EBFA;\n90\t  --gold: #C98A3B;\n91\t  --gold-dark: #9C6723;\n92\t  --ink: #1F1626;\n93\t  --muted: #5a5064;\n94\t  --border: #E4DCEC;\n95\t  --paper: #FDFBFE;\n96\t  --panel: #FFFFFF;\n97\t  --danger: #B3261E;\n98\t  --danger-dark: #8C1D16;\n99\t  --danger-bg: #FBE9E4;\n100\t  --success-bg: #E3F3EF;\n101\t  --success-border: #2E7D6B;\n102\t}\n103\t* { box-sizing: border-box; }\n104\thtml { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; }\n105\tbody {\n106\t  font: 16px/1.6 \"Inter\", system-ui, sans-serif;\n107\t  margin: 0;\n108\t  color: var(--ink);\n109\t  background: var(--paper);\n110\t  overflow-wrap: anywhere;\n111\t}\n112\th1, h2 { font-family: \"Fraunces\", Georgia, serif; Every\n`app/routes/*.py` module except `public.py` uses this (the public site has\nits own, unrelated live-preview chrome in `app/routes/public.py`).\n\nIssue #13: the admin console's stylesheet link is relative and\ndepth-computed (see app.services.css_path) rather than root-absolute —\na literal `href=\"/...\"` would still work on this live server, but\n`scripts/check_submission.py` greps every tracked template for\nroot-absolute paths regardless of whether the page is ever statically\nexported, so this stays relative like everything else.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom urllib.parse import quote\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import models\nfrom app.routes.auth import ensure_csrf_token\nfrom app.services.css_path import css_path_for\n\nSIDEBAR = [\n    (\"/admin/dashboard\", \"Dashboard\"),\n    (\"/admin/content\", \"Content list\"),\n    (\"/admin/pending\", \"Pending queue\"),\n    (\"/admin/accounts\", \"Accounts\"),\n    (\"/admin/pages\", \"Page hierarchy\"),\n    (\"/admin/tags\", \"Tags\"),\n    (\"/admin/metrics\", \"Metrics\"),\n]\n\nEDITOR_SIDEBAR = [\n    (\"/admin\", \"My posts\"),\n]\n\n\ndef console_context(request: Request, user: models.User, sidebar=None) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"The csrf token, stylesheet path, and sidebar every authenticated\n    admin screen needs. Defaults the sidebar by role (Staff vs Ambassador)\n    so most call sites don't have to pick one themselves.\"\"\"\n    chosen = sidebar or (SIDEBAR if user.role == \"admin\" else EDITOR_SIDEBAR)\n    return {\n        \"user\": user,\n        \"csrf_token\": ensure_csrf_token(request),\n        \"css_path\": css_path_for(request),\n        \"sidebar\": [{\"href\": href, \"label\": label} for href, label in chosen],\n    }\n\n\ndef redirect_with_flash(\n    url: str, message: str, *, fragment: str | None = None, **extra_params: str\n) -> RedirectResponse:\n    \"\"\"A 303 redirect carrying a one-time success message, read back by\n    templates/base.html's `request.query_params`. No session state: a\n    refresh of the destination page just drops the message, which is fine\n    for a \"your save worked\" banner.\n\n    `fragment` and `extra_params` (#15 follow-up) let a caller land the\n    reader on a specific part of a long page — e.g. an image upload redirect\n    jumps straight to that upload section instead of the top of the post\n    form, with `extra_params` carrying which Media was just added so the\n    template can show its thumbnail there. The fragment is appended last,\n    since a URL fragment must come after the query string to be valid.\n    \"\"\"\n    sep = \"&\" if \"?\" in url else \"?\"\n    target = f\"{url}{sep}flash={quote(message)}\"\n    for key, value in extra_params.items():\n        target += f\"&{key}={quote(str(value))}\"\n    if fragment:\n        target += f\"#{fragment}\"\n    return RedirectResponse(url=target, status_code=303)\n\n\n# Reuses the public site's Kenyon purple + gold palette and Fraunces/Inter\n# fonts (app/publish.py's CSS) for a consistent look, but is otherwise\n# self-contained: the admin console's HTML (sidebar, forms, plain <ul> lists\n# standing in for tables) is different enough from the public site's that\n# sharing one stylesheet would mean every admin rule risks colliding with a\n# public one, or vice versa.\nADMIN_CSS = \"\"\"/* Admin console shell — issue #13. Same palette/fonts as the\n   public site (app/publish.py's CSS), different components: a sidebar\n   layout, plain lists standing in for tables, and HTML forms. */\n:root {\n  color-scheme: light dark;\n  --purple: #5B2A86;\n  --purple-dark: #3E1C5E;\n  --purple-light: #F2EBFA;\n  --gold: #C98A3B;\n  --gold-dark: #9C6723;\n  --ink: #1F1626;\n  --muted: #5a5064;\n  --border: #E4DCEC;\n  --paper: #FDFBFE;\n  --panel: #FFFFFF;\n  --danger: #B3261E;\n  --danger-dark: #8C1D16;\n  --danger-bg: #FBE9E4;\n  --success-bg: #E3F3EF;\n  --success-border: #2E7D6B;\n}\n* { box-sizing: border-box; }\nhtml { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; }\nbody {\n  font: 16px/1.6 \"Inter\", system-ui, sans-serif;\n  margin: 0;\n  color: var(--ink);\n  background: var(--paper);\n  overflow-wrap: anywhere;\n}\nh1, h2 { font-family: \"Fraunces\", Georgia, serif; }\n\nheader.site-header {\n  background: var(--purple);\n  padding: 0.85rem 1.5rem;\n}\nheader.site-header .brand {\n  color: #fff;\n  font-family: \"Fraunces\", Georgia, serif;\n  font-weight: 600;\n  font-size: 1.1rem;\n}\nmain { padding: 1.5rem; }\n/* The just-added confirmation (redirected back from a successful upload,\n   console_shell.redirect_with_flash's `fragment`/`added_media_id`): the\n   usual flash banner plus a small thumbnail of the image itself. */\n.upload-added { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem; }\n.upload-added img {\n  width: 2.75rem;\n  height: 2.75rem;\n  object-fit: cover;\n  border-radius: 0.3rem;\n  flex-shrink: 0;\n}\n\n/* -- formatting help (#15 follow-up) ------------------------------------ */\n/* A small Markdown cheat-sheet next to the body field (templates/admin/\n   posts_form.html), for students who have never seen Markdown before.\n   Open by default via <details open>; the summary doubles as a Hide/Show\n   toggle with no JS needed, via the [open] attribute selector below. */\n.formatting-help {\n  border: 1px solid var(--border);\n  border-radius: 0.6rem;\n  padding: 0.5rem 1.25rem;\n  margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\n  background: #fff;\n}\n.formatting-help summary {\n  cursor: pointer;\n  font-weight: 600;\n  display: flex;\n  justify-content: space-between;\n}\n.formatting-help summary::after {\n  content: \"Show\";\n  font-weight: 400;\n  color: var(--muted);\n}\n.formatting-help[open] summary::after { content: \"Hide\"; }\n.formatting-help ul { margin: 0.5rem 0; padding-left: 1.25rem; }\n.formatting-help .help-note { color: var(--muted); }\n/* The \"You type\" -> \"You get\" table: the right column is real sanitized\n   HTML (app.services.markdown.formatting_help_examples), so it can never\n   show formatting the sanitizer wouldn't actually allow. */\n.formatting-table {\n  width: 100%;\n  border-collapse: collapse;\n  margin: 0.75rem 0;\n}\n.formatting-table th, .formatting-table td {\n  text-align: left;\n  vertical-align: top;\n  padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem;\n  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);\n}\n.formatting-table td:first-child code { white-space: pre-line; }\n.formatting-table td:last-child :first-child { margin-top: 0; }\n.formatting-table td:last-child :last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }\n\n/* -- lists standing in for tables --------------------------------------- */\nul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }\nmain ul li {\n  display: flex;\n  flex-wrap: wrap;\n  align-items: center;\n  gap: 0.6rem;\n  padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem;\n  border: 1px solid var(--border);\n  border-radius: 0.5rem;\n  margin: 0 0 0.6rem;\n  background: #fff;\n}\nmain ul li form { margin: 0; }\n\n/* The Page hierarchy tree nests arbitrarily deep — indent it instead of\n   boxing every level like a flat row list. */\n.page-tree, .page-tree ul { padding-left: 0; }\n.page-tree li, .page-tree li li {\n  display: block;\n  border: none;\n  background: none;\n  padding: 0.3rem 0 0.3rem 0.9rem;\n  margin: 0;\n  border-left: 2px solid var(--border);\n}\n\n/* -- the Staff/Ambassador console shell --------------------------------- */\n.console { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 0; }\n.console-sidebar {\n  flex: 0 0 15rem;\n  background: var(--purple-light);\n  border-radius: 0.6rem;\n  padding: 1.1rem;\n  margin-right: 1.75rem;\n}\n.console-sidebar p { margin: 0 0 0.6rem; }\n.console-main { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }\n\n@media (max-width: 30rem) {\n  main { padding: 1rem; }\n  .console { flex-direction: column; }\n  .console-sidebar { flex: none; width: 100%; margin: 0 0 1.25rem; {"parentUuid":"7e36d39f-68d4-4224-ad16-a7ec616fccec","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"247f2c90-5919-414c-bd75-f9027d24d908","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DQUpKjhBPLJ4PWGJiY9tAt","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The admin console's relative stylesheet path, computed per-request.\n2\t\n3\tSplit out of app/services/console_shell.py so app/routes/auth.py (login,\n4\tthe pre-login \"hello\" screen) can use it without a circular import:\n5\tconsole_shell already imports ensure_csrf_token from auth, so auth can't\n6\timport console_shell back.\n7\t\"\"\"\n8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n9\t\n10\tfrom fastapi import Request\n11\t\n12\t\n13\tdef css_path_for(request: Request) -> str:\n14\t    \"\"\"The live admin server has no static-file route tied to a page's own\n15\t    nesting depth — /admin/posts/{id}/edit and /login sit at different\n16\t    depths — so this computes the right number of \"../\" to reach the one\n17\t    GET /style.css route (app/routes/console.py) from wherever `request`\n18\t    currently is. Same idea as app.publish's `_relative_link` for the\n19\t    static export, just computed per-request instead of precomputed per\n20\t    chain.\"\"\"\n21\t    depth = len([s for s in request.url.path.strip(\"/\").split(\"/\") if s]) - 1\n22\t    return \"../\" * max(depth, 0) + \"style.css\"\n23\t"}]},"uuid":"6cadfd95-520b-4a82-94bb-0618b7776f32","timestamp":"2026-10-08T18:49:57.796Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/services/css_path.py","content":"\"\"\"The admin console's relative stylesheet path, computed per-request.\n\nSplit out of app/services/console_shell.py so app/routes/auth.py (login,\nthe pre-login \"hello\" screen) can use it without a circular import:\nconsole_shell already imports ensure_csrf_token from auth, so auth can't\nimport console_shell back.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\n\n\ndef css_path_for(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The live admin server has no static-file route tied to a page's own\n    nesting depth — /admin/posts/{id}/edit and /login sit at different\n    depths — so this computes the right number of \"../\" to reach the one\n    GET /style.css route (app/routes/console.py) from wherever `request`\n    currently is. Same idea as app.publish's `_relative_link` for the\n    static export, just computed per-request instead of precomputed per\n    chain.\"\"\"\n    depth = len([s for s in request.url.path.strip(\"/\").split(\"/\") if s]) - 1\n    return \"../\" * max(depth, 0) + \"style.css\"\n","numLines":23,"startLine":1,"totalLines":23}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"7e36d39f-68d4-4224-ad16-a7ec616fccec","session_id":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, media, pages, posts, public, tags\nfrom app.routes.auth import AdminRequired, CsrfInvalid, LoginRequired\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    db.init_db()\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                        session_cookie=\"cms_session\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def _login_required(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(url=\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(AdminRequired)\n    def _admin_required(request: Request, exc: AdminRequired):\n        return PlainTextResponse(\"Forbidden\", status_code=403)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(CsrfInvalid)\n    def _csrf_invalid(request: Request, exc: CsrfInvalid):\n        return PlainTextResponse(\"Forbidden: missing or invalid CSRF token\", status_code=403)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(tags.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(media.router)\n\n    # Catch-all last: the live public site, read straight from the database —\n    # the admin console's \"preview\" of what `cms publish` will later export.\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":7,"newStart":15,"newLines":8,"lines":[" "," from app import db, settings"," from app.routes import accounts, auth, console, media, pages, posts, public, tags","-from app.routes.auth import AdminRequired, CsrfInvalid, LoginRequired","+from app.routes.auth import AdminRequired, CsrfInvalid, LoginRequired, get_current_user, templates","+from app.services.css_path import css_path_for"," "," "," def create_app() -> FastAPI:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"982b7011-7510-471e-83fb-7d252aac710e","session_id":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

Catch-all last: the live public site, read straight from the database —\n54\t    # the admin console's \"preview\" of what `cms publish` will later export.\n55\t    app.include_router(public.router)\n56\t    return app\n57\t\n58\t\n59\tapp = create_app()\n60\t"}]},"uuid":"f3dc31b6-420f-46c2-a9f7-c6462bd0eab8","timestamp":"2026-10-08T18:50:38.475Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/main.py","content":"\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, media, pages, posts, public, tags\nfrom app.routes.auth import AdminRequired, CsrfInvalid, LoginRequired, get_current_user, templates\nfrom app.services.css_path import css_path_for\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    db.init_db()\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                        session_cookie=\"cms_session\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def _login_required(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(url=\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(AdminRequired)\n    def _admin_required(request: Request, exc: AdminRequired):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/forbidden.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Staff only\", \"user\": get_current_user(request),\n             \"css_path\": css_path_for(request)},\n            status_code=403,\n        )\n\n    @app.exception_handler(CsrfInvalid)\n    def _csrf_invalid(request: Request, exc: CsrfInvalid):\n        return PlainTextResponse(\"Forbidden: missing or invalid CSRF token\", status_code=403)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(tags.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(media.router)\n\n    # Catch-all last: the live public site, read straight from the database —\n    # the admin console's \"preview\" of what `cms publish` will later export.\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","numLines":60,"startLine":1,"totalLines":60}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0a6d3e60-1257-40c6-959b-71b71977774f","session_id":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"322e1dd4-0d47-4b33-90d2-0e14f6568875","version":"2.1.272","gitBranch":"main"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"d05358d6-d941-4c0a-9edf-a78ca35d6b78","timestamp":"2026-10-08T18:51:03.625Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/main.py","oldString":"            {\"title\": \"Staff only\", \"user\": get_current_user(request),\n             \"css_path\": css_path_for(request)},","newString":"            {\"title\": \"Staff only\", \"user\": get_current_user(request),\n             \"css_path\": css_path_for(request), \"my_posts_href\": \"/admin\"},","originalFile":"\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, media, pages, posts, public, tags\nfrom app.routes.auth import AdminRequired, CsrfInvalid, LoginRequired, get_current_user, templates\nfrom app.services.css_path import css_path_for\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    db.init_db()\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                        session_cookie=\"cms_session\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def _login_required(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(url=\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(AdminRequired)\n    def _admin_required(request: Request, exc: AdminRequired):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/forbidden.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Staff only\", \"user\": get_current_user(request),\n             \"css_path\": css_path_for(request)},\n            status_code=403,\n        )\n\n    @app.exception_handler(CsrfInvalid)\n    def _csrf_invalid(request: Request, exc: CsrfInvalid):\n        return PlainTextResponse(\"Forbidden: missing or invalid CSRF token\", status_code=403)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(pages.router)\n    app.include_router(posts.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(tags.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(media.router)\n\n    # (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"3e0689d3-eaaa-44e1-bdad-5abfed47e17a","timestamp":"2026-10-08T19:44:30.094Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/README.md","oldString":"| anthropic | Test | 2 | a fake row from an Oct 1 ledger test, not real usage — left in `notes/usage-ledger.csv` rather than edit graded evidence |\n\nNo non-Anthropic backend","newString":"| anthropic | Test | 2 | a fake row from an Oct 1 ledger test, not real usage — left in `notes/usage-ledger.csv` rather than edit graded evidence |\n| anthropic | Claude (claude.ai chat) | not in ledger | step-by-step guidance and drafting prompts for Claude Code; not tracked by the usage ledger |\n\nNo non-Anthropic backend","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nA small web CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE)'s study\nabroad blog (IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2). A local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja\n+ SQLite) is where Staff and Ambassadors write and review content; `cms publish`\nrenders only the published content into `site/` as static HTML, deployed to\nGitHub Pages. The admin console itself never goes on the public internet.\n\nClaude Code was used throughout this project. I took more of a manager and planner's role: answering the grill questions and overriding Claude on a number of occasions, reading and criticizing the spec, checking results and editing until the desired outcome was achieved, and pushing for specific designs that I had in my mind. I picked the stretch goals myself, and added to each of the other goals as well. Throughout the process, I updated CLAUDE.md and set rules to ensure that we were moving through the project in a way that was aligned with my intentions. I also tested the site as a user, allowing me to suggest edits and critique from the position of somebody using my product. I used chat Claude in my browser to assist with prompt engineering and project organization/management, and I used Claude Code to build the tool itself. \n\n## Live URL\n\nPublic site: https://adamleidercollege-code.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\nRepo: https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms\n\n## Features\n\nThe 7 required capabilities, built for this client:\n\n1. **Login** — Staff and Ambassadors sign in and out; passwords hashed with argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.\n2. **Two roles** — **Staff** (`admin`) and **Ambassador** (`editor`), with genuinely different permissions: Staff can do everything an Ambassador can, plus publish, manage users, and manage the page tree.\n3. **Posts** — full CRUD; title, auto-generated slug (frozen once published), Markdown body, draft → pending → published status, author, timestamps, one Topic, any number of Tags.\n4. **Pages** — a Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, plus standalone pages (About, Contact); published pages appear in the public nav and breadcrumbs.\n5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a filterable content list, a post editor with a live preview, and a page editor. \n6. **User management** — Staff-only: create users, change roles, deactivate/reactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in, and deactivation rules differ by role (an Ambassador's drafts are deleted, a Staff member's are kept).\n7. **Public site and publish** — only published content reaches `site/`; Markdown is sanitized before render; nav is built from published pages; `cms publish` writes relative paths only.\n\nStretch features added beyond the required 7:\n\n- **Tags** — Staff-only creation, filterable within a Program, independent of Topic.\n- **Search** — runs entirely client-side from a JSON index built at publish time, scoped to a section or sitewide, so it works on GitHub Pages with no server.\n- **Media** — post covers and inline images set by the author; program covers set by Staff; uploads are resized, rotated upright, and stripped of EXIF/GPS data.\n- **Formatting help** — a \"You type → You get\" Markdown help box in the post and page editors, for Ambassadors who don't already know Markdown.\n\n## Run locally\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\ncd iphs400-mp2-cms\nuv sync\ncp .env.example .env\nuv run python scripts/seed_demo.py   # optional: seeds demo Staff/Ambassador accounts and sample content\nuv run cms serve                     # http://localhost:8000/admin\n```\n\nDemo accounts created by the seed script (from `.env.example`'s default passwords):\n`admin@example.test` / `change-me-admin` (Staff), `editor@example.test` / `change-me-editor` (Ambassador).\n\nRun the test suite with `uv run pytest -q`.\n\nVerified 2026-10-08 on a fresh clone in a scratch directory: `uv sync`, `cp .env.example .env`,\nand `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` all ran unmodified; `uv run pytest -q` passed 226/226;\n`uv run cms serve` came up clean and `/` and `/admin` both returned HTTP 200. Nothing failed.\n\nTo publish the public site from what's currently published in the database:\n\n```bash\nuv run cms publish   # writes site/\nuv run cms deploy    # pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch\n```\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\nWhile I made the majority of design decisions in this project, Claude did help with some things. The structure of the site, such as the names of the roles, the site tree design, the overall structure, the formatting help box for markdown in the post section, locked slugs once published, most of the design details like those were decided by me, with Claude making the smaller implementation and coding decisions. For a number of these implementations, Claude suggested a plan, and I edited or changed it (editable to permanent slugs (because ambassadors won't know what a slug is), staff work being kept after their accounts get deactivated). Claude did solve a few problems I wouldn't have noticed otherwise, like implementation problems that I have little experience with, such as two staff members potentially working on and publishing the same post at once. Overall, I made the majority of design decisions and Claude implemented them, but there was some crossover on both sides. \n\n### Models and skills used\n\nBuilt with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Anthropic), using these\nClaude Code skills throughout the grill → spec → tickets → implement → review loop:\n`/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`,\n`/handoff`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n### Backends used\n\n| Provider | Model | Ledger rows | Used for |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| anthropic | Sonnet 5 | 190 | grill, spec, tickets, implementation, review, and deploy — nearly the whole project |\n| anthropic | Opus 5 | 4 | setup and the T11 design pass (better design taste, but burned the 5-hour usage window much faster than Sonnet) |\n| anthropic | Test | 2 | a fake row from an Oct 1 ledger test, not real usage — left in `notes/usage-ledger.csv` rather than edit graded evidence |\n\nNo non-Anthropic backend (e.g. OpenRouter, Z.ai) was used anywhere in this project — every row in the ledger is `anthropic`.\n\n### Two prompts I actually sent\n\nPrompt 1 (grill answer A3, session 16):\n\n> A CGE staff member should be able to write posts as well if they desire; they should have all the tools the ambassador role has. The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\n\nPrompt 2 (test seams, before `/to-spec`):\n\n> Those two seams match was I was expecting, but could you also do a third one: a small services layer for the pure rules like slug generation, the status transitions (who can move a post from a draft to pending to published and back), and what happens to an ambassadors posts when they're deactivated. Those rules are really the core of how the CGE's review works, so I want them to be tested directly as opposed to only through HTTP, and this will keep the code splits into models, routes, templates, and services.\n\n### Real model failures\n\n- Claude ran the submission checker with the wrong Python, reported a test failure that wasn't real, then caught and corrected it.\n- `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` skipped creating the spec/ticket/stretch labels the project needed.\n- `/code-review`'s background fork hung 36+ minutes (T03); Claude then reviewed its own code, breaking the \"reviewer ≠ author\" rule. Rerunning with a fresh foreground subagent fixed it.\n- A `/loop` wakeup kept re-firing after tickets were done, re-prompting Claude for nothing.\n- Claude committed T07 but didn't push, so issue #8 stayed open.\n- Claude said it couldn't take screenshots until Playwright was installed for it.\n- While verifying flash messages, Claude created a stray \"Flash Test\" account in the real local demo database instead of a test copy. It caught and deleted it before the screenshots.\n- Claude (chat) stated that \"Add image\" inserts the Markdown line for you, as fact, before checking; when asked, it admitted it was inferring. It turned out to be true, but it was verified before writing the help box around it.\n- The admin console was never styled (`style.css` 404 on every nested admin page) through the entire build; nothing caught it — not the tests, not any review — until the required screenshots were taken (#13).\n\nThe failure that mattered the most to me was probably the review hang. The review hung and ran for 36 minutes, which first took a great deal of my time, but second, after the review hung, Claude proceeded to review its own code without an external reviewer. The external review function exists to ensure security and efficiency - if a Claude agent reviews its own work, it's much more likely to approve it. Fortunately, the issue was caught and I reran the code review with a fresh subagent, subsequently adding a CLAUDE.md rule to always run reviews that way, which later caught a number of real bugs, such as the race condition, the footer bug, and the PR #17 image leak.
