{"parentUuid":"9787cbfa-9936-4af5-acb3-b637e44a20f5","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"cff188db-ee94-4843-a0c5-ab207f0a45f6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BGpktW6gDGGi4Cc2z413jY","type":"tool_result","content":"commit e512d1562471a3b402fed5fe3f780f99c4f4e8b6\nAuthor: Adam Leider <adamleidercollege@gmail.com>\nDate:   Thu Oct 8 15:45:43 2026 -0400\n\n    Add claude.ai chat row to README Backends used table\n    \n    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n\ndiff --git a/README.md b/README.md\nindex f864082..6dfae1e 100644\n--- a/README.md\n+++ b/README.md\n@@ -1,45 +1,107 @@\n-# IPHS 400 — Mini-Project #2 starter (Web CMS)\n+# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n \n-Click **Use this template** → name your repo **`iphs400-mp2-cms`** → make it **Public**.\n-Do not fork: a fork arrives without an Issues tab, and your tickets live in Issues.\n+A small web CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE)'s study\n+abroad blog (IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2). A local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja\n++ SQLite) is where Staff and Ambassadors write and review content; `cms publish`\n+renders only the published content into `site/` as static HTML, deployed to\n+GitHub Pages. The admin console itself never goes on the public internet.\n \n-## Start here\n+Claude Code was used throughout this project. I took more of a manager and planner's role: answering the grill questions and overriding Claude on a number of occasions, reading and criticizing the spec, checking results and editing until the desired outcome was achieved, and pushing for specific designs that I had in my mind. I picked the stretch goals myself, and added to each of the other goals as well. Throughout the process, I updated CLAUDE.md and set rules to ensure that we were moving through the project in a way that was aligned with my intentions. I also tested the site as a user, allowing me to suggest edits and critique from the position of somebody using my product. I used chat Claude in my browser to assist with prompt engineering and project organization/management, and I used Claude Code to build the tool itself. \n \n-1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. Read Part 0 and Part 1 first.\n-2. `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` — how you are graded. Read it **before** you build.\n-3. `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` — Exercise A, in Part 4 of the manual.\n+## Live URL\n \n-## Run it\n+Public site: https://adamleidercollege-code.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n+\n+Repo: https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms\n+\n+## Features\n+\n+The 7 required capabilities, built for this client:\n+\n+1. **Login** — Staff and Ambassadors sign in and out; passwords hashed with argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.\n+2. **Two roles** — **Staff** (`admin`) and **Ambassador** (`editor`), with genuinely different permissions: Staff can do everything an Ambassador can, plus publish, manage users, and manage the page tree.\n+3. **Posts** — full CRUD; title, auto-generated slug (frozen once published), Markdown body, draft → pending → published status, author, timestamps, one Topic, any number of Tags.\n+4. **Pages** — a Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, plus standalone pages (About, Contact); published pages appear in the public nav and breadcrumbs.\n+5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a filterable content list, a post editor with a live preview, and a page editor. \n+6. **User management** — Staff-only: create users, change roles, deactivate/reactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in, and deactivation rules differ by role (an Ambassador's drafts are deleted, a Staff member's are kept).\n+7. **Public site and publish** — only published content reaches `site/`; Markdown is sanitized before render; nav is built from published pages; `cms publish` writes relative paths only.\n+\n+Stretch features added beyond the required 7:\n+\n+- **Tags** — Staff-only creation, filterable within a Program, independent of Topic.\n+- **Search** — runs entirely client-side from a JSON index built at publish time, scoped to a section or sitewide, so it works on GitHub Pages with no server.\n+- **Media** — post covers and inline images set by the author; program covers set by Staff; uploads are resized, rotated upright, and stripped of EXIF/GPS data.\n+- **Formatting help** — a \"You type → You get\" Markdown help box in the post and page editors, for Ambassadors who don't already know Markdown.\n+\n+## Run locally\n \n ```bash\n+git clone https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\n+cd iphs400-mp2-cms\n uv sync\n cp .env.example .env\n-uv run cms serve        # then open http://localhost:8000/admin  -> \"T00: hello admin\"\n+uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py   # optional: seeds demo Staff/Ambassador accounts and sample content\n+uv run cms serve                     # http://localhost:8000/admin\n ```\n \n-## What is here\n+Demo accounts created by the seed script (from `.env.example`'s default passwords):\n+`admin@example.test` / `change-me-admin` (Staff), `editor@example.test` / `change-me-editor` (Ambassador).\n+\n+Run the test suite with `uv run pytest -q`.\n+\n+Verified 2026-10-08 on a fresh clone in a scratch directory: `uv sync`, `cp .env.example .env`,\n+and `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` all ran unmodified; `uv run pytest -q` passed 226/226;\n+`uv run cms serve` came up clean and `/` and `/admin` both returned HTTP 200. Nothing failed.\n \n-```text\n-.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger (Exercise A lives in ctx_guard.py)\n-scripts/           usage_report.py (Exercise B lives in spend()), check_submission.py, seed_demo.py\n-tests/             the exercise tests, plus helpers such as client_as(\"editor\")\n-app/, templates/   the T00 skeleton — every CMS feature is yours to build\n-docs/adr/          two example decision records\n+To publish the public site from what's currently published in the database:\n+\n+```bash\n+uv run cms publish   # writes site/\n+uv run cms deploy    # pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch\n ```\n \n-Two functions are deliberately unfinished and their tests fail until you write them:\n-`decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` and `spend()` in `scripts/usage_report.py`.\n-Both are graded. Use `/tdd`, as the manual says.\n+## Generative AI Use Statement\n \n-## Deadlines\n+While I made the majority of design decisions in this project, Claude did help with some things. The structure of the site, such as the names of the roles, the site tree design, the overall structure, the formatting help box for markdown in the post section, locked slugs once published, most of the design details like those were decided by me, with Claude making the smaller implementation and coding decisions. For a number of these implementations, Claude suggested a plan, and I edited or changed it (editable to permanent slugs (because ambassadors won't know what a slug is), staff work being kept after their accounts get deactivated). Claude did solve a few problems I wouldn't have noticed otherwise, like implementation problems that I have little experience with, such as two staff members potentially working on and publishing the same post at once. Overall, I made the majority of design decisions and Claude implemented them, but there was some crossover on both sides. \n \n-Stage 1 (`mp2-mvp` tag): Tue Sep 29, 2:40 pm Eastern (soft target).\n-Stage 2 (`mp2-final` tag): Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern, grace until Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm.\n+### Models and skills used\n \n-Run `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n+Built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Anthropic), using these\n+Claude Code skills throughout the grill → spec → tickets → implement → review loop:\n+`/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`,\n+`/handoff`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n \n-## Generative AI Use Statement\n+### Backends used\n+\n+| Provider | Model | Ledger rows | Used for |\n+|---|---|---|---|\n+| anthropic | Sonnet 5 | 190 | grill, spec, tickets, implementation, review, and deploy — nearly the whole project |\n+| anthropic | Opus 5 | 4 | setup and the T11 design pass (better design taste, but burned the 5-hour usage window much faster than Sonnet) |\n+| anthropic | Test | 2 | a fake row from an Oct 1 ledger test, not real usage — left in `notes/usage-ledger.csv` rather than edit graded evidence |\n+| anthropic | Claude (claude.ai chat) | not in ledger | step-by-step guidance and drafting prompts for Claude Code; not tracked by the usage ledger |\n+\n+No non-Anthropic backend (e.g. OpenRouter, Z.ai) was used anywhere in this project — every row in the ledger is `anthropic`.\n+\n+### Two prompts I actually sent\n+\n+Prompt 1 (grill answer A3, session 16):\n+\n+> A CGE staff member should be able to write posts as well if they desire; they should have all the tools the ambassador role has. The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\n+\n+Prompt 2 (test seams, before `/to-spec`):\n+\n+> Those two seams match was I was expecting, but could you also do a third one: a small services layer for the pure rules like slug generation, the status transitions (who can move a post from a draft to pending to published and back), and what happens to an ambassadors posts when they're deactivated. Those rules are really the core of how the CGE's review works, so I want them to be tested directly as opposed to only through HTTP, and this will keep the code splits into models, routes, templates, and services.\n+\n+### Real model failures\n+\n+- Claude ran the submission checker with the wrong Python, reported a test failure that wasn't real, then caught and corrected it.\n+- `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` skipped creating the spec/ticket/stretch labels the project needed.\n+- `/code-review`'s background fork hung 36+ minutes (T03); Claude then reviewed its own code, breaking the \"reviewer ≠ author\" rule. Rerunning with a fresh foreground subagent fixed it.\n+- A `/loop` wakeup kept re-firing after tickets were done, re-prompting Claude for nothing.\n+- Claude committed T07 but didn't push, so issue #8 stayed open.\n+- Claude said it couldn't take screenshots until Playwright was installed for it.\n+- While verifying flash messages, Claude created a stray \"Flash Test\" account in the real local demo database instead of a test copy. It caught and deleted it before the screenshots.\n+- Claude (chat) stated that \"Add image\" inserts the Markdown line for you, as fact, before checking; when asked, it admitted it was inferring. It turned out to be true, but it was verified before writing the help box around it.\n+- The admin console was never styled (`style.css` 404 on every nested admin page) through the entire build; nothing caught it — not the tests, not any review — until the required screenshots were taken (#13).\n \n-*(Required. Replace this section: name the models and skills you used, quote two\n-prompts you really sent, describe one real model failure, and include a\n-\"Backends used\" table if you ever switched providers.)*\n+The failure that mattered the most to me was probably the review hang. The review hung and ran for 36 minutes, which first took a great deal of my time, but second, after the review hung, Claude proceeded to review its own code without an external reviewer. The external review function exists to ensure security and efficiency - if a Claude agent reviews its own work, it's much more likely to approve it. passwords hashed with argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.\n+2. **Two roles** — **Staff** (`admin`) and **Ambassador** (`editor`), with genuinely different permissions: Staff can do everything an Ambassador can, plus publish, manage users, and manage the page tree.\n+3. **Posts** — full CRUD; published pages appear in the public nav and breadcrumbs.\n+5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a filterable content list, a post editor with a live preview, and a page editor. \n+6. **User management** — Staff-only: create users, change roles, deactivate/reactivate; {"parentUuid":"5c528e0d-2247-417b-8a8c-0df892904fd6","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/README.md","snippet":"1\t# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n2\t\n3\tA small web CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE)'s study\n4\tabroad blog (IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2). A local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja\n5\t+ SQLite) is where Staff and Ambassadors write and review content; `cms publish`\n6\trenders only the published content into `site/` as static HTML, deployed to\n7\tGitHub Pages. The admin console itself never goes on the public internet.\n8\t\n9\tClaude Code was used throughout this project. I took more of a manager and planner's role: answering the grill questions and overriding Claude on a number of occasions, reading and criticizing the spec, checking results and editing until the desired outcome was achieved, and pushing for specific designs that I had in my mind. I picked the stretch goals myself, and added to each of the other goals as well. Throughout the process, I updated CLAUDE.md and set rules to ensure that we were moving through the project in a way that was aligned with my intentions. I also tested the site as a user, allowing me to suggest edits and critique from the position of somebody using my product. I used chat Claude in my browser to assist with prompt engineering and project organization/management, and I used Claude Code to build the tool itself. \n10\t\n11\t## Live URL\n12\t\n13\tPublic site: https://adamleidercollege-code.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n14\t\n15\tRepo: https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms\n16\t\n17\t## Features\n18\t\n19\tThe 7 required capabilities, built for this client:\n20\t\n21\t1. **Login** — Staff and Ambassadors sign in and out; passwords hashed with argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.\n22\t2. **Two roles** — **Staff** (`admin`) and **Ambassador** (`editor`), with genuinely different permissions: Staff can do everything an Ambassador can, plus publish, manage users, and manage the page tree.\n23\t3. **Posts** — full CRUD; title, auto-generated slug (frozen once published), Markdown body, draft → pending → published status, author, timestamps, one Topic, any number of Tags.\n24\t4. **Pages** — a Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, plus standalone pages (About, Contact); published pages appear in the public nav and breadcrumbs.\n25\t5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a filterable content list, a post editor with a live preview, and a page editor. \n26\t6. **User management** — Staff-only: create users, change roles, deactivate/reactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in, and deactivation rules differ by role (an Ambassador's drafts are deleted, a Staff member's are kept).\n27\t7. **Public site and publish** — only published content reaches `site/`; Markdown is sanitized before render; nav is built from published pages; `cms publish` writes relative paths only.\n28\t\n29\tStretch features added beyond the required 7:\n30\t\n31\t- **Tags** — Staff-only creation, filterable within a Program, independent of Topic.\n32\t- **Search** — runs entirely client-side from a JSON index built at publish time, scoped to a section or sitewide, so it works on GitHub Pages with no server.\n33\t- **Media** — post covers and inline images set by the author; program covers set by Staff; uploads are resized, rotated upright, and stripped of EXIF/GPS data.\n34\t- **Formatting help** — a \"You type → You get\" Markdown help box in the post and page editors, for Ambassadors who don't already know Markdown.\n35\t\n36\t## Run locally\n37\t\n38\t```bash\n39\tgit clone https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\n40\tcd iphs400-mp2-cms\n41\tuv sync\n42\tcp .env.example .env\n43\tuv run python scripts/seed_demo.py   # optional: seeds demo Staff/Ambassador accounts and sample content\n44\tuv run cms serve                     # http://localhost:8000/admin\n45\t```\n46\t\n47\tDemo accounts created by the seed script (from `.env.example`'s default passwords):\n48\t`admin@example.test` / `change-me-admin` (Staff), `editor@example.test` / `change-me-editor` (Ambassador).\n49\t\n50\tRun the test suite with `uv run pytest -q`.\n51\t\n52\tVerified 2026-10-08 on a fresh clone in a scratch directory: `uv sync`, `cp .env.example .env`,\n53\tand `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` all ran unmodified; `uv run pytest -q` passed 226/226;\n54\t`uv run cms serve` came up clean and `/` and `/admin` both returned HTTP 200. Nothing failed.\n55\t\n56\tTo publish the public site from what's currently published in the database:\n57\t\n58\t```bash\n59\tuv run cms publish   # writes site/\n60\tuv run cms deploy    # pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch\n61\t```\n62\t\n63\t## Generative AI Use Statement\n64\t\n65\tWhile I made the majority of design decisions in this project, Claude did help with some things. The structure of the site, such as the names of the roles, the site tree design, the overall structure, the formatting help box for markdown in the post section, locked slugs once published, most of the design details like those were decided by me, with Claude making the smaller implementation and coding decisions. For a number of these implementations, Claude suggested a plan, and I edited or changed it (editable to permanent slugs (because ambassadors won't know what a slug is), staff work being kept after their accounts get deactivated). Claude did solve a few problems I wouldn't have noticed otherwise, like implementation problems that I have little experience with, such as two staff members potentially working on and publishing the same post at once. Overall, I made the majority of design decisions and Claude implemented them, but there was some crossover on both sides. \n66\t\n67\t### Models and skills used\n68\t\n69\tBuilt with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Anthropic), using these\n70\tClaude Code skills throughout the grill → spec → tickets → implement → review loop:\n71\t`/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`,\n72\t`/handoff`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n73\t\n74\t### Backends used\n75\t\n76\t| Provider | Model | Ledger rows | Used for |\n77\t|---|---|---|---|\n78\t| anthropic | Sonnet 5 | 190 | grill, spec, tickets, implementation, review, and deploy — nearly the whole project |\n79\t| anthropic | Opus 5 | 4 | setup and the T11 design pass (better design taste, but burned the 5-hour usage window much faster than Sonnet) |\n80\t| anthropic | Test | 2 | a fake row from an Oct 1 ledger test, not real usage — left in `notes/usage-ledger.csv` rather than edit graded evidence |\n81\t| anthropic | Opus 5.5 (claude.ai chat) | not in ledger | step-by-step guidance and drafting prompts for Claude Code; not tracked by the usage ledger |\n82\t\n83\tNo non-Anthropic backend (e.g. OpenRouter, Z.ai) was used anywhere in this project — every row in the ledger is `anthropic`.\n84\t\n85\t### Two prompts I actually sent\n86\t\n87\tPrompt 1 (grill answer A3, session 16):\n88\t\n89\t> A CGE staff member should be able to write posts as well if they desire; they should have all the tools the ambassador role has. The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\n90\t\n91\tPrompt 2 (test seams, before `/to-spec`):\n92\t\n93\t> Those two seams match was I was expecting, but could you also do a third one: a small services layer for the pure rules like slug generation, the status transitions (who can move a post from a draft to pending to published and back), and what happens to an ambassadors posts when they're deactivated. Those rules are really the core of how the CGE's review works, so I want them to be tested directly as opposed to only through HTTP, and this will keep the code splits into models, routes, templates, and services.\n94\t\n95\t### Real model failures\n96\t\n97\t- Claude ran the submission checker with the wrong Python, reported a test failure that wasn't real, then caught and corrected it.\n98\t- `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` skipped creating the spec/ticket/stretch labels the project needed.\n99\t- `/code-review`'s background fork hung 36+ minutes (T03); Claude then reviewed its own code, breaking the \"reviewer ≠ author\" rule. Rerunning with a fresh foreground subagent fixed it.\n100\t- A `/loop` wakeup kept re-firing after tickets were done, re-prompting Claude for nothing.\n\n... {"parentUuid":"9a43509f-bf09-493b-adc5-2db89e2b7c98","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f1ac04bd-1277-4605-af0b-3d33ee84b354","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DVvd4yyV3RPpZhXmTqpM29","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/README.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"c04f54a1-ec50-4d44-bf1f-990376caa88a","timestamp":"2026-10-08T21:03:20.574Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/README.md","oldString":"`/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`,\n`/handoff`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.","newString":"`/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`,\n`/handoff`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `/wait-what`, `/ask-matt`.","originalFile":"# Kenyon CGE Study Abroad CMS\n\nA small web CMS built for the Kenyon Center for Global Engagement (CGE)'s study\nabroad blog (IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2). A local admin console (FastAPI + Jinja\n+ SQLite) is where Staff and Ambassadors write and review content; `cms publish`\nrenders only the published content into `site/` as static HTML, deployed to\nGitHub Pages. The admin console itself never goes on the public internet.\n\nClaude Code was used throughout this project. I took more of a manager and planner's role: answering the grill questions and overriding Claude on a number of occasions, reading and criticizing the spec, checking results and editing until the desired outcome was achieved, and pushing for specific designs that I had in my mind. I picked the stretch goals myself, and added to each of the other goals as well. Throughout the process, I updated CLAUDE.md and set rules to ensure that we were moving through the project in a way that was aligned with my intentions. I also tested the site as a user, allowing me to suggest edits and critique from the position of somebody using my product. I used chat Claude in my browser to assist with prompt engineering and project organization/management, and I used Claude Code to build the tool itself. \n\n## Live URL\n\nPublic site: https://adamleidercollege-code.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\nRepo: https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms\n\n## Features\n\nThe 7 required capabilities, built for this client:\n\n1. **Login** — Staff and Ambassadors sign in and out; passwords hashed with argon2, never stored or logged in plain text.\n2. **Two roles** — **Staff** (`admin`) and **Ambassador** (`editor`), with genuinely different permissions: Staff can do everything an Ambassador can, plus publish, manage users, and manage the page tree.\n3. **Posts** — full CRUD; title, auto-generated slug (frozen once published), Markdown body, draft → pending → published status, author, timestamps, one Topic, any number of Tags.\n4. **Pages** — a Continent → Country → Program tree below Home, plus standalone pages (About, Contact); published pages appear in the public nav and breadcrumbs.\n5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a filterable content list, a post editor with a live preview, and a page editor. \n6. **User management** — Staff-only: create users, change roles, deactivate/reactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in, and deactivation rules differ by role (an Ambassador's drafts are deleted, a Staff member's are kept).\n7. **Public site and publish** — only published content reaches `site/`; Markdown is sanitized before render; nav is built from published pages; `cms publish` writes relative paths only.\n\nStretch features added beyond the required 7:\n\n- **Tags** — Staff-only creation, filterable within a Program, independent of Topic.\n- **Search** — runs entirely client-side from a JSON index built at publish time, scoped to a section or sitewide, so it works on GitHub Pages with no server.\n- **Media** — post covers and inline images set by the author; program covers set by Staff; uploads are resized, rotated upright, and stripped of EXIF/GPS data.\n- **Formatting help** — a \"You type → You get\" Markdown help box in the post and page editors, for Ambassadors who don't already know Markdown.\n\n## Run locally\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/adamleidercollege-code/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\ncd iphs400-mp2-cms\nuv sync\ncp .env.example .env\nuv run python scripts/seed_demo.py   # optional: seeds demo Staff/Ambassador accounts and sample content\nuv run cms serve                     # http://localhost:8000/admin\n```\n\nDemo accounts created by the seed script (from `.env.example`'s default passwords):\n`admin@example.test` / `change-me-admin` (Staff), `editor@example.test` / `change-me-editor` (Ambassador).\n\nRun the test suite with `uv run pytest -q`.\n\nVerified 2026-10-08 on a fresh clone in a scratch directory: `uv sync`, `cp .env.example .env`,\nand `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` all ran unmodified; `uv run pytest -q` passed 226/226;\n`uv run cms serve` came up clean and `/` and `/admin` both returned HTTP 200. Nothing failed.\n\nTo publish the public site from what's currently published in the database:\n\n```bash\nuv run cms publish   # writes site/\nuv run cms deploy    # pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch\n```\n\n## Generative AI Use Statement\n\nWhile I made the majority of design decisions in this project, Claude did help with some things. The structure of the site, such as the names of the roles, the site tree design, the overall structure, the formatting help box for markdown in the post section, locked slugs once published, most of the design details like those were decided by me, with Claude making the smaller implementation and coding decisions. For a number of these implementations, Claude suggested a plan, and I edited or changed it (editable to permanent slugs (because ambassadors won't know what a slug is), staff work being kept after their accounts get deactivated). Claude did solve a few problems I wouldn't have noticed otherwise, like implementation problems that I have little experience with, such as two staff members potentially working on and publishing the same post at once. Overall, I made the majority of design decisions and Claude implemented them, but there was some crossover on both sides. \n\n### Models and skills used\n\nBuilt with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Anthropic), using these\nClaude Code skills throughout the grill → spec → tickets → implement → review loop:\n`/grill-with-docs`, `/to-spec`, `/to-tickets`, `/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`,\n`/handoff`, `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n### Backends used\n\n| Provider | Model | Ledger rows | Used for |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| anthropic | Sonnet 5 | 190 | grill, spec, tickets, implementation, review, and deploy — nearly the whole project |\n| anthropic | Opus 5 | 4 | setup and the T11 design pass (better design taste, but burned the 5-hour usage window much faster than Sonnet) |\n| anthropic | Test | 2 | a fake row from an Oct 1 ledger test, not real usage — left in `notes/usage-ledger.csv` rather than edit graded evidence |\n| anthropic | Opus 5.5 (claude.ai chat) | not in ledger | step-by-step guidance and drafting prompts for Claude Code; not tracked by the usage ledger |\n\nNo non-Anthropic backend (e.g. OpenRouter, Z.ai) was used anywhere in this project — every row in the ledger is `anthropic`.\n\n### Two prompts I actually sent\n\nPrompt 1 (grill answer A3, session 16):\n\n> A CGE staff member should be able to write posts as well if they desire; they should have all the tools the ambassador role has. The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\n\nPrompt 2 (test seams, before `/to-spec`):\n\n> Those two seams match was I was expecting, but could you also do a third one: a small services layer for the pure rules like slug generation, the status transitions (who can move a post from a draft to pending to published and back), and what happens to an ambassadors posts when they're deactivated. Those rules are really the core of how the CGE's review works, so I want them to be tested directly as opposed to only through HTTP, and this will keep the code splits into models, routes, templates, and services.\n\n### Real model failures\n\n- Claude ran the submission checker with the wrong Python, reported a test failure that wasn't real, then caught and corrected it.\n- `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` skipped creating the spec/ticket/stretch labels the project needed.\n- `/code-review`'s background fork hung 36+ minutes (T03); Claude then reviewed its own code, breaking the \"reviewer ≠ author\" rule. Rerunning with a fresh foreground subagent fixed it.\n- A `/loop` wakeup kept re-firing after tickets were done, re-prompting Claude for nothing.\n- Claude committed T07 but didn't push, so issue #8 stayed open.\n- Claude said it couldn't take screenshots until Playwright was installed for it.\n- While verifying flash messages, Claude created a stray \"Flash Test\" account in the real local demo database instead of a test copy. It caught and deleted it before the screenshots.\n- Claude (chat) stated that \"Add image\" inserts the Markdown line for you, as fact, before checking; when asked, it admitted it was inferring. It turned out to be true, but it was verified before writing the help box around it.\n- The admin console was never styled (`style.css` 404 on every nested admin page) through the entire build; nothing caught it — not the tests, not any review — until the required screenshots were taken (#13).\n\nThe failure that mattered the most to me was probably the review hang. The review hung and ran for 36 minutes, which first took a great deal of my time, but second, after the review hung, Claude proceeded to review its own code without an external reviewer. The external review function exists to ensure security and efficiency - if a Claude agent reviews its own work, it's much more likely to approve it. Fortunately, the issue was caught and I reran the code review with a fresh subagent, subsequently adding a CLAUDE.md rule to always run reviews that way, which later caught a number of real bugs, such as the race condition, the footer bug, and the PR #17 image leak. {"parentUuid":"d5f0b90a-938a-4b3e-93d5-febee44c8fd1","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/home/adam_leider/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/report-notes.md","snippet":"1\t# Report notes\n2\t\n3\t## Q1: What I built + grill decisions that were MINE\n4\t- Client: Kenyon CGE study abroad blog (picked it because I'm going to DIS Copenhagen in spring).\n5\t- Overrode Claude:\n6\t  - Q3: Claude wanted \"CGE staff\"/\"student ambassador\" as words to AVOID. I kept Staff/Ambassador as the UI names (admin/editor in code).\n7\t  - Q10: Claude recommended editable slugs. I said auto-generated and NOT editable (ambassadors won't know what a slug is), frozen once published.\n8\t  - Q12: Kept the WordPress-style landing (site preview as home, sidebar tabs) instead of a plain dashboard page.\n9\t  - Spec flag 3: Claude assumed Staff drafts get deleted on deactivation like Ambassadors'. I changed it so Staff drafts are kept.\n10\t- My own additions: pending \"submit for review\" status, Continent→Country→Program page tree with demo data, topics on posts with a filter, footer pages (About/Contact), nav bar + breadcrumbs, ambassador drafts deleted when deactivated, \"are you sure?\" before delete.\n11\t- Added later as stretch: tags, search, media uploads, and a Formatting help box for students who don't know Markdown.\n12\t- Scope cuts I chose: trash/auto-delete, scheduled publishing, suggested edits, messaging/comments (all need a live server or extra features). Search was kept as a stretch ticket and later built (#10).\n13\t\n14\t## Q2: Drift (what the AI made up + what caught it)\n15\t- Spec #1: Claude filled in decisions I never made (slug -2/-3 suffixes, Staff can't publish others' drafts directly, Staff drafts deleted on deactivation). Caught by reading the spec before tickets.\n16\t- T01 (#2): code showed raw role codes \"admin/editor\" in the UI instead of Staff/Ambassador from CONTEXT.md. Caught by /code-review. Fixed with User.role_label.\n17\t- Design passes (T11): Claude started calling posts \"dispatches\" in the hero, footer and headings. Not in CONTEXT.md, where the term is \"Post\". I caught it by reading the live site and had it changed to match the glossary.\n18\t- The admin console had never loaded its stylesheet (relative \"style.css\" 404'd on every nested admin page). Every ticket's tests and reviews passed anyway; it was only caught when taking the required screenshots. Fixed under its own issue, #13.\n19\t- PR #17 (media): review caught that a post could reference another post's or a draft's image ID, leaking unpublished images to the public site. Fixed before merge.\n20\t\n21\t## Q3: Skills, prompts, resources\n22\t- Skills: /grill-with-docs, /to-spec, /to-tickets, /implement, /tdd, /code-review, /handoff, /setup-matt-pocock-skills, /wait-what, /ask-matt\n23\t\n24\t- Prompts I actually used (quote these word for word in the README):\n25\t  - Prompt 1 (grill answer A3, session 16):\n26\t    \"A CGE staff member should be able to write posts as well if they desire; they should have all the tools the ambassador role has. The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\"\n27\t  - Prompt 2 (test seams, before /to-spec):\n28\t    \"Those two seams match was I was expecting, but could you also do a third one: a small services layer for the pure rules like slug generation, the status transitions (who can move a post from a draft to pending to published and back), and what happens to an ambassadors posts when they're deactivated. Those rules are really the core of how the CGE's review works, so I want them to be tested directly as opposed to only through HTTP, and this will keep the code splits into models, routes, templates, and services.\"\n29\t  - How I started: the /grill-with-docs kickoff for the CGE study abroad blog (mostly drafted with help).\n30\t\n31\t## Q4: Budget + what I'd add next\n32\t- Plan said opusplan/Opus high for grill/spec/tickets. Ledger shows it ran on Sonnet 5 high. I believe my computer restarted and I forgot to shift the model back when I began again.\n33\t- usage_report.py after T01 (Oct 5, 2:11 am):\n34\t\n35\t      phase          turns  5h spent   weekly  models / provider\n36\t      T01                4      4.0%     0.0%  Sonnet 5\n37\t      grill             14     23.0%     6.0%  Sonnet 5\n38\t      setup             14     16.0%    14.0%  Opus 5,Sonnet 5,Test\n39\t      spec               4      4.0%     1.0%  Sonnet 5\n40\t      tickets            3      4.0%     1.0%  Sonnet 5\n41\t      unlabelled        16     10.0%     2.0%  Sonnet 5\n42\t\n43\t      Tickets done: 1 · average weekly cost per ticket: 0.0%\n44\t      Forecast: 7 tickets need ~0% of the weekly cap; 62% remains → FITS\n45\t\n46\t- Plan vs actual: planned 30% of a 5h window per ticket (20 implement + 10 review); T01 actually cost 4%. Grill planned 30%, actual 23%. I overestimated tickets by a lot.\n47\t- The \"0% weekly per ticket\" is a rounding artifact: the weekly meter only moves in whole numbers, so T01 cost under 1%, not zero.\n48\t- The \"Test\" model in the setup row is a fake test row from Oct 1, not real usage. I left it in the ledger rather than edit graded evidence.\n49\t- 16 turns are \"unlabelled\" because I didn't always set the phase before starting work.\n50\t- usage_report.py after T03 (Oct 5, 5 pm):\n51\t  - T01 5% of a 5h window / 1% weekly · T02 17% / 5% · T03 15% / 2%\n52\t  - Avg ~12% of a window and 2.7% weekly per ticket, vs my plan of 30% per ticket. I overestimated by more than half.\n53\t  - T02 cost the most (four review fixes + first deploy). T03's hung review added cost too.\n54\t  - Forecast: 5 tickets need ~13% of the weekly cap, 54% remains → FITS.\n55\t- Next: trash with restore, scheduled publishing, suggested edits, private messaging, visitor accounts, search filters by views, a Preview pane for the page editor (the post editor has one). See notes/future-work.md.\n56\t- Considered adding comments, view counts, visitor accounts and private messaging after the core build, but they all need a live server. Free hosting tiers wipe the SQLite database on sleep (Render's free Postgres also expires after 30 days), and paid hosting is ~$4–5/month (Fly.io) plus the security, moderation and student-privacy responsibilities. Kept them as future work; giscus (GitHub Discussions) comments would be the cheapest first step.\n57\t\n58\t## Real model failures (README needs at least 1)\n59\t- Claude ran the submission checker with the wrong Python, reported a test failure that wasn't real, then caught and corrected it.\n60\t- /setup-matt-pocock-skills skipped creating the spec/ticket/stretch labels the project needed.\n61\t- /code-review's background fork hung 36+ min (T03); Claude then reviewed its own code. Rerunning with a fresh foreground subagent fixed it.\n62\t- A /loop wakeup kept re-firing after tickets were done, re-prompting Claude for nothing.\n63\t- Claude committed T07 but didn't push, so issue #8 stayed open. Added a CLAUDE.md rule to push and confirm CLOSED.\n64\t- Claude said it couldn't take screenshots until I had it install Playwright.\n65\t- While verifying flash messages, Claude created a stray \"Flash Test\" account in my real local demo database instead of a test copy. It caught and deleted it before the screenshots.\n66\t- Claude (chat) told me \"Add image\" inserts the Markdown line for you as if it were fact before checking; I asked, and it admitted it was inferring. It turned out to be true (it appends to the end), but I had it verified before writing the help box around it.\n67\t- #13: the admin console was never styled (style.css 404) through the whole build; nobody noticed until the screenshot step.\n68\t\n69\t## Things that went wrong (good for report voice)\n70\t- Grill session crashed twice; recovered with claude --resume / fg after accidentally hitting Ctrl+Z.\n71\t- Did the grill in an Orca worktree on a side branch by accident; had to merge it into main.\n72\t- Transcripts were saving as \"your-name\": the template had no CMS_STUDENT setting. Fixed in .env/.env.example.\n73\t- Found settings.json had the context warnings lowered to 30/40%; reverted to the course's 50/60/80.\n74\t\n75\t## T02 (#3)\n\n... The role names shown in the site and CONTEXT.md can be Staff and Ambassador, but in the code they stay admin (Staff) and editor (Ambassador).\"\n27\t  - Prompt 2 (test seams, before /to-spec):\n28\t    \"Those two seams match was I was expecting, but could you also do a third one: a small services layer for the pure rules like slug generation, the status transitions (who can move a post from a draft to pending to published and back), and what happens to an ambassadors posts when they're deactivated. Those rules are really the core of how the CGE's review works, so I want them to be tested directly as opposed to only through HTTP, and this will keep the code splits into models, routes, templates, and services.\"\n29\t  - How I started: the /grill-with-docs kickoff for the CGE study abroad blog (mostly drafted with help).\n30\t\n31\t## Q4: Budget + what I'd add next\n32\t- Plan said opusplan/Opus high for grill/spec/tickets. Ledger shows it ran on Sonnet 5 high. I believe my computer restarted and I forgot to shift the model back when I began again.\n33\t- usage_report.py after T01 (Oct 5, 2:11 am):\n34\t\n35\t      phase          turns  5h spent   weekly  models / provider\n36\t      T01                4      4.0%     0.0%  Sonnet 5\n37\t      grill             14     23.0%     6.0%  Sonnet 5\n38\t      setup             14     16.0%    14.0%  Opus 5,Sonnet 5,Test\n39\t      spec               4      4.0%     1.0%  Sonnet 5\n40\t      tickets            3      4.0%     1.0%  Sonnet 5\n41\t      unlabelled        16     10.0%     2.0%  Sonnet 5\n42\t\n43\t      Tickets done: 1 · average weekly cost per ticket: 0.0%\n44\t      Forecast: 7 tickets need ~0% of the weekly cap; 62% remains → FITS\n45\t\n46\t- Plan vs actual: planned 30% of a 5h window per ticket (20 implement + 10 review); T01 actually cost 4%. Grill planned 30%, actual 23%. I overestimated tickets by a lot.\n47\t- The \"0% weekly per ticket\" is a rounding artifact: the weekly meter only moves in whole numbers, so T01 cost under 1%, not zero.\n48\t- The \"Test\" model in the setup row is a fake test row from Oct 1, not real usage. I left it in the ledger rather than edit graded evidence.\n49\t- 16 turns are \"unlabelled\" because I didn't always set the phase before starting work.\n50\t- usage_report.py after T03 (Oct 5, 5 pm):\n51\t  - T01 5% of a 5h window / 1% weekly · T02 17% / 5% · T03 15% / 2%\n52\t  - Avg ~12% of a window and 2.7% weekly per ticket, vs my plan of 30% per ticket. I overestimated by more than half.\n53\t  - T02 cost the most (four review fixes + first deploy). T03's hung review added cost too.\n54\t  - Forecast: 5 tickets need ~13% of the weekly cap, 54% remains → FITS.\n55\t- Next: trash with restore, scheduled publishing, suggested edits, private messaging, visitor accounts, search filters by views, a Preview pane for the page editor (the post editor has one). See notes/future-work.md.\n56\t- Considered adding comments, view counts, visitor accounts and private messaging after the core build, but they all need a live server. Free hosting tiers wipe the SQLite database on sleep (Render's free Postgres also expires after 30 days), and paid hosting is ~$4–5/month (Fly.io) plus the security, moderation and student-privacy responsibilities. Kept them as future work; giscus (GitHub Discussions) comments would be the cheapest first step.\n57\t\n58\t## Real model failures (README needs at least 1)\n59\t- Claude ran the submission checker with the wrong Python, reported a test failure that wasn't real, then caught and corrected it.\n60\t- /setup-matt-pocock-skills skipped creating the spec/ticket/stretch labels the project needed.\n61\t- /code-review's background fork hung 36+ min (T03); Claude then reviewed its own code. It turned out to be true (it appends to the end), but I had it verified before writing the help box around it.\n67\t- #13: the admin console was never styled (style.css 404) through the whole build; nobody noticed until the screenshot step.\n68\t\n69\t## Things that went wrong (good for report voice)\n70\t- Grill session crashed twice; recovered with claude --resume / fg after accidentally hitting Ctrl+Z.\n71\t- Did the grill in an Orca worktree on a side branch by accident; had to merge it into main.\n72\t- Transcripts were saving as \"your-name\": the template had no CMS_STUDENT setting. Fixed in .env/.env.example.\n73\t- Found settings.json had the context warnings lowered to 30/40%; reverted to the course's 50/60/80.\n74\t\n75\t## T02 (#3)\n\n...
